original_record.question: A marble with radius $15 \mathrm{~cm}$ fits exactly under a cone as shown in the diagram. The slant height of the cone is equal to the diameter of its base. What is the height of the cone in $\mathrm{cm}$ ? <image1>
original_record.solution: Because the slant height of the cone is the same as the diameter of its base, the cross-section of the cone is an equilateral triangle, as shown. The cross-section of the sphere is the incircle of the triangle and has radius $15 \mathrm{~cm}$. By the symmetry of the figure $\angle P O R=360^{\circ} \div 6=60^{\circ}$, and hence, triangle $P O R$ has angles $90^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}$ (so it is half of an equilateral triangle). Hence $O R$ is twice $O P$ and  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-138.jpg?height=314&width=350&top_left_y=2219&top_left_x=1479) hence is $30 \mathrm{~cm}$. Since $O T=O R$, it follows that $P T$ is $15+30=45 \mathrm{~cm}$. This is the height of the cone.  [Alternatively: You may know that the medians of a triangle intersect at one third of their heights, so $O P=15 \mathrm{~cm}$ is one third of the height.]
